proof_review.finding: The actual joint-feature representation supplies the specific hf and hRep for the literal predictor and data integral. The Gaussian smooth ridge is pulled back along Prod.fst via its measure-preserving linear isometry. The actual toLp map F is definitionally aligned with that pullback; the rfl step uses the same pointwise polynomial and proof-irrelevant membership witnesses, not an arbitrary feature. No response differentiability or higher label moments are assumed.

hV extracts the exact integral-potential identity from hRep. L_rho is twice the inner-product functional of the actual feature mean minus the L2 label, so V_rho=L_rho composed with F. Continuous-linear composition proves ambient C-infinity. The law-probability premise remains on each use of hRep; total Bochner notation alone is not used as an integrability proof.

Compactness of the ambient closed unit ball bounds the fixed continuous feature by B. B is nonnegative because zero lies in that ball, including zero dimension. Integrating the sphere restriction against any probability gives one mean bound; the triangle inequality and the norm of innerSL give the common residual-functional bound 2*(B+norm(label)). B and the bound do not depend on rho.

Each finite order n lies below smooth infinity in the actual nested infinity type. Continuity of its iterated derivative on a compact closed ball supplies C before rho and w. max(C,0) gives a nonnegative bound even for empty negative-radius balls. The genuine Mathlib norm_iteratedFDeriv_comp_left theorem and monotone multiplication finish the uniform bound, including n=0. No desired derivative estimate is a binder.

definition_and_domain_review: V is the literal actual joint-data double integral with factor 2. Gaussianity applies only to the input marginal; the response may be dependent and non-Gaussian.
The only label condition is L2. Parent representation proves actual product integrability; L2 multiplication is used for scalar integrability, not an unsupported L2-times-L2-to-L2 rule.
All spatial evaluation points are ambient. The averaging law lives on the unit sphere. This result does not rely on a unit-only Gram identity or differentiate such an identity off its domain.
iteratedFDeriv uses total derivatives, but the separately proved C-infinity conclusion makes them classical throughout E for each probability rho. The derivative is not divided by a factorial.

n=0 is the function-value norm. R may be negative or zero. E may have dimension zero, in which case there is no sphere probability instance. Arbitrary signed coefficients and constant/zero polynomials are included.
The constant may depend on E, P, p, R and n. It is chosen before rho and w, and no explicit numerical or dimension-free constant is asserted.
